kwargs.profile_path: Required. The Hermes home that owns the kanban store: the shared default home (profile["path"] in audit_surface, i.e. hermes_constants.get_hermes_home()). Kanban lives in the shared default home, not in a named profile; pass the default home when the active profile is a named one. No config.yaml or credential file is read; the module is self-contained.
kwargs.db_path: Do not pass in the runner (default None = <profile_path>/kanban.db). Offline-copy override for a renamed database inside profile_path; a path outside it is refused (outside_profile).
kwargs.reference_time: Do not pass in the runner (default None). Ages are then relative to each board's newest event, so the section is digest-stable. Passing a wall-clock value (e.g. as_of) would make ages run-dependent; when given it is echoed only in run_metrics.reference_time_override and the section says reference_clock="injected".
kwargs.home_path: Do not pass in the runner (default None = profile_path). Offline-copy only: maps the original absolute home prefix stored in task workspace paths of an extracted copy onto profile_path.
kwargs.clock: Do not pass in the runner (default time.monotonic). Test hook for the 15-second cooperative budget; only run_metrics.elapsed_seconds depends on it.

consequences.kanban_residue.agent_authored_board: At least 80% of a board's tasks, on a board of 20 or more tasks, carry an agent-side author marker (worker, decomposer or a profile that ran tasks); the marker names the writing surface, not who asked for the work, and work done through the default chat profile counts as user-side.
consequences.kanban_residue.archived_never_collected: Archived tasks still keep their logs and all their rows: more than 1,000,000 bytes of archived-task logs, or a board at least 80% archived with events more than 30 days older than its newest event; the audit cannot tell whether clean-up was ever run.
consequences.kanban_residue.blocked_loops: At least one task has four or more runs with no completed run or reached Hermes's repeated-block limit of 2; these are stored records of past attempts, not a current fault, and do not show whether another attempt would succeed.
consequences.kanban_residue.could_not_verify: Some kanban measurements could not be verified within the supported schema and read budgets; missing coverage is not a clean result.
consequences.kanban_residue.heartbeat_bloat: More than half of a board's stored events, on a board of 500 or more events, are worker heartbeats; this counts retained rows, not whether the work made progress.
consequences.kanban_residue.machine_paths_in_tasks: More than half of a board's task bodies or of its comments contain a home-style absolute path marker; this counts text markers, not whether those paths exist on this machine.
consequences.kanban_residue.never_run_backlog: More than 10% of a board's tasks have no recorded run and were created more than seven days before the reference time; this counts stored rows, not why they never ran.
consequences.kanban_residue.orphan_board_folders: One or more board folders hold board metadata but no database; the audit does not tell how they came to be that way.
consequences.kanban_residue.retry_context_growth: Rebuilt from text stored today, a retried task would hand its latest worker more characters of its own body, comments and earlier attempts than at its first run, above the review limit of 20,000 characters or three times the first-run figure; Hermes caps each item but not the total. The first-run figure uses today's body and is an estimate when the body was edited after that run. This is a reconstruction from stored rows, not a recording of any prompt, and it describes left-over data, not a current fault.
consequences.kanban_residue.workspaces_inside_home: Five or more tasks store a workspace path inside the Hermes home but outside Hermes's own kanban workspaces folder; this counts stored paths, not files that are safe to delete.

free_strings.what: boards[].path: absolute path of the board database file that was opened (<profile>/kanban.db, <profile>/kanban/boards/<slug>/kanban.db or <profile>/kanban/boards/_archived/<slug>-<epoch>/kanban.db; or the db_path override inside the home)
free_strings.why_safe: Found by lstat inside profile_path with no symlink component and not credential-named; depth is fixed (at most four levels under the home); it is the board identity the user needs. The serializer keeps it as the resolved absolute path when it exists at sealing time (tested); if it vanished before sealing it becomes a per-run token.

free_strings.what: finding source_paths[].path: the same absolute board database path for board findings; <profile>/kanban/boards for orphan_board_folders; the vocabulary label kanban.db for could_not_verify
free_strings.why_safe: Same rule as boards[].path; persistence pick(source_paths) serializes it with the same scalar rule and keeps it unchanged (tested).

notes: adapt_component_result keeps run_metrics: every top-level key other than ok/status/error/findings/coverage/classification is copied through unchanged (contract.py:615-617). status is the legacy 'pass'/'fail' from make_component_envelope and is recorded only as legacy_status_ignored. commit_unit_result/component_dto does NOT persist run_metrics or the section: the caller must pick result['kanban_residue'] into finalize_run(measurements=...) (and add 'kanban_residue' to the names loop in store.finalize_run, which today copies only skill_hygiene/write_settings/session_contamination) and keep result['run_metrics'] outside the digested payload.
Call: _component('kanban_residue', identity, kanban_residue.audit_kanban_residue, profile_path=<shared default Hermes home>) in full-home mode only. Pass no other kwargs.

Dict keys: the caller must add every schema_keys entry to SCHEMA_KEYS (task status and run outcome labels are dict KEYS of tasks_by_status / runs_by_outcome; agent/user/unclassified are keys of authorship.tasks/comments). Unknown keys are replaced by 'hmac:<digest>' SealedKeys, including the section key 'kanban_residue' itself (tested as control).

Values: every vocabulary entry must be in VOCABULARY; rule ids are needed in RULE_IDS (else the finding id itself is hashed in the DTO, tested as control) and the ten sentences in FINDING_CONSEQUENCES (else persistence substitutes DEFAULT_FINDING_CONSEQUENCE). Finding evidence is flat numbers/booleans only; all of numeric_evidence_keys must be in _EVIDENCE_NUMERIC_KEYS or persistence drops them. No vocab evidence keys.

Free strings: only kept absolute paths (boards[].path, finding source_paths[].path). EvidenceSerializer.scalar returns Path(value).resolve() when it lstat's: unchanged when the home path has no symlinked component (tests use a real tmp_path); if the audited home is reached through a symlinked directory the stored path is its resolved form; if the database vanished before sealing it becomes a per-run token. Board slugs, task IDs, workspace folder names, titles, authors and sessions never leave the module.

Behaviour changes made for wiring: (1) a board held open by a running Hermes (-wal with frames + existing -shm) is now read mode=ro like every other audited DB (only -shm read marks may change); -wal with frames and no -shm -> wal_needs_index; rollback journal -> hot_journal; database_in_use now means SQLite busy/locked only. (2) consequences are fixed sentences; numbers moved to flat evidence. (3) section: boards carry a kind label (default/named_board) plus the absolute database path instead of the slug; top_tasks/growth_example no longer carry task_id; machine_binding.workspace_samples removed (counts kept); date_range is [YYYYMM, YYYYMM] integers; '<unsafe-name>' placeholder no longer emitted.

Known limit: task_id (t_ + 8 hex, Hermes-generated) was removed because the serializer would hash it per run; restoring it for 'hermes kanban show <id>' guidance would need a key-specific serializer rule for task_id matching ^t_[0-9a-f]{8}$.

Digest: with reference_time unset, ages are relative to each board's newest event and the section is identical across runs (tested with clocks days apart and with two serializers/run keys). Only the time_budget cut (15 cooperative seconds) can differ between runs on a slow machine; it is reported as coverage could_not_verify. finding_dto adds a keyed source_digest to every finding of every section; the tests exclude it as not section data.

Unreached in tests: truncated_by database_changed (mid-read writer race) and unreadable (OS permission error); every other vocabulary token is produced by a synthetic home and checked by the strict walker.
